trial_court: Court of Sh. Surinder S. Rathi, District Judge (Comm.)-03 Shahdara, KKD, Delhi
case_name: Icici Bank Ltd vs Kapil Kumar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: ICICI Bank Limited, a nationalized bank (plaintiff)
parties.respondent_defendant: Kapil Kumar, s/o Sh. Ramesh Chandra (defendant)

facts_of_case: Defendant approached ICICI Bank for an auto loan to purchase a Honda City Car. The loan was sanctioned but the defendant defaulted on payments. ICICI Bank issued a foreclosure notice and filed this suit to recover the outstanding amount.

legal_principles.principle: Where any party from whom a written statement is required fails to present the same within the time permitted, the Court shall pronounce judgment against him, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit.
legal_principles.held: The Court shall pronounce judgment against him, or make such order in relation to the suit as it thinks fit
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 8 Rule 10

legal_principles.principle: In the absence of any pleadings on behalf of the defendant, the case of the plaintiff is deemed to be admitted.
legal_principles.held: The pleadings of the plaintiff has remained unrebutted, unchallenged and uncontroverted
cited_cases: ICICI Bank Ltd. Vs. Kapil Kumar

legal_principles.principle: The Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as it deems reasonable to be paid on the principal sum adjudged.
legal_principles.held: The Court may, in the decree, order interest at such rate as it deems reasonable to be paid on the principal sum adjudged

outcome.final_order: The court decreed in favour of ICICI Bank, ordering the recovery of Rs.8,60,840/- along with interest @24% per annum from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount.

use_for_drafting: practical tips for advocates in debt recovery cases
